kept.excerpt: Datafolha reported Eduardo Paes at 47% of valid first-round votes and Douglas Ruas at 35%, compared with 51% and 23%, respectively, in August. In the scenario excluding Garotinho, Paes had 48% and Ruas 38%. The survey conducted 1,204 in-person interviews in 35 municipalities from September 29 to October 1 and was registered under RJ-02070/2026 and BR-01272/2026. The institute reported that 27% of voters could still change their vote.
kept.relevance: The latest dated primary poll available at the cutoff shows Ruas gaining substantially while still trailing Paes, with meaningful remaining voter uncertainty.

kept.excerpt: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on October 2 put Eduardo Paes at 41.9% of first-round voting intentions and Douglas Ruas at 30.1%. Anthony Garotinho had 8.2%, while each remaining candidate registered no more than 1.9%.
kept.relevance: A separate polling institute corroborates Paes's lead over Ruas immediately before the election and documents Garotinho's potentially consequential vote share.

kept.excerpt: Atlas/Estadão recorded Eduardo Paes at 44.1% and Douglas Ruas at 35.7% of first-round voting intentions, compared with 45.7% and 32.4% in its previous release. In the hypothetical runoff, Paes had 51.1% and Ruas 42.1%, equivalent to 54.9% and 45.1% of valid votes. The survey interviewed 1,836 voters through random digital recruitment from September 22 to 27, with a two-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence. Its TSE registration was RJ-09456/2026.
kept.relevance: This poll supplies both a narrowing first-round trend and a direct runoff comparison using a different collection method.

kept.excerpt: Quaest put Eduardo Paes at 34% and Douglas Ruas at 25% in the first round; without Garotinho, the figures were 35% and 26%. In a hypothetical runoff, Paes led Ruas by 43% to 33%, compared with 44% to 31% previously. Quaest conducted 1,302 household interviews from September 25 to 28, with a three-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence. The poll was registered under RJ-04419/2026.
kept.relevance: Quaest provides another independent poll family showing Ruas narrowing the gap while trailing in both rounds.

kept.excerpt: TSE minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques determined on October 2 that votes for Rio gubernatorial candidate Anthony Garotinho should be considered null. The decision stated that votes for him would be classified as 'anulados sub judice' under the currently effective refusal of his candidacy registration, even though his name would appear on voting machines. The minister revoked the earlier injunction that had protected his candidacy prerogatives.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day legal development affects the treatment of a third candidate's votes and therefore the valid-vote denominator used to determine whether a runoff is required.

kept.excerpt: On September 11, the TRE-RJ unanimously refused Anthony Garotinho's registration as a gubernatorial candidate because of missing eligibility conditions and a statutory ineligibility ground. The court cited a conviction for intentional administrative misconduct involving damage to public funds and illicit enrichment of third parties, which expressly suspended his political rights. The decision could be appealed to the TSE.
kept.publisher: Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Rio de Janeiro (TRE-RJ)
kept.relevance: The official court account establishes the legal basis of the candidacy dispute underlying the October 2 ruling.

kept.excerpt: TSE Resolution 23.760 of March 2, 2026 establishes the electoral calendar for the 2026 elections. The calendar schedules the first round for October 4 and the second round, where necessary, for October 25. The elections include the offices of state governor and vice-governor.
kept.publisher: Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Diário da Justiça Eletrônico
kept.relevance: The official published calendar verifies the election being forecast and its scheduled rounds.

search_notes: Frozen evidence pack for Q085, with an inclusive publication cutoff of 2026-10-02. Excerpts are factual English translations or close paraphrases of Portuguese source passages. Dates were verified from publication timestamps or official dated publication records exposed by web_search; timestamps use the sources' Brazilian local time where shown. CNN's October 2 legal report also showed an update on October 2 at 21:56, within the cutoff. The official calendar publication date follows its March 4 Diário da Justiça record, distinct from the resolution's March 2 adoption date. web_fetch failed because of a provider configuration error; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval was unavailable and evidence was restricted to dated source passages returned by web_search. Unknown-date pages, later publications, retrospective election aggregators, prediction-market and betting pages were excluded. Multiple reports of the same poll were consolidated; the four polling items represent different institutes. No post-cutoff developments or election outcomes are included.
